 3m ago 04.41 EDT 8th over: England 41-0 (Banton 41, Duckett 5) Fernando changes ends to replace Madushanka. Banton doesn’t care who’s bowling. He stands tall to slice a drive through backward point for four, then clatters another boundary through mid-off.
 Two months ago, Ben Duckett and Jacob Bethell were England’s preferred opening partnership for the World Cup; right now they feel like rivals for a place alongside Banton.
 “I’m (almost) simultaneously working on a Lingala-English dictionary, reading Geoff Lemon describing the weather in South Africa, and looking at your Eng vs Sri Lanka OBO,” writes John Stedman. “The latter is by far the most boring – not due to your scintillating commentary, of course, but because tri-series seem so pointless, whereas the Test match in SA is gripping. Just an opinion.”
 I prefer tri-series to bilateral fixtures. That aside, I’m nodding like a Wackeldackel.
 Share Updated at  04.41 EDT 9m ago 04.35 EDT 7th over: England 37-0 (Banton 32, Duckett 4) Eshan Malinga, nephew of, replaces Asitha Fernando and starts with a wide. Banton plays another beautiful stroke, pushing a boundary to the left of mid-on. His timing has been exquisite, and in this form he looks undroppable.
 “Good morning,” writes John Starbuck. “Yes, there are some of us following the action; you are not typing into a void just yet.”
 Yet . (NB: clip contains some effin’ and jeffin’.)
 Share 15m ago 04.30 EDT 6th over: England 31-0 (Banton 28, Duckett 3) Banton continues to go after Madushanka, slapping a short ball for four and timing another boundary through extra cover off the back foot. #TopBants
 The scorecard looks lopsided but Banton has monopolised the strike: Duckett has faced only eight of the 36 deliveries.
 Share 19m ago 04.25 EDT 5th over: England 23-0 (Banton 20, Duckett 3) Banton takes a pair of twos and a single from Asitha Fernando’s third over. He’s off to another good start, 20 from 22 balls, and will be keen to cash in after throwing away a potential century on Tuesday.
 Share 22m ago 04.22 EDT The latest from Gqerberha (spoiler: rain) 
 South Africa v Australia: second men’s cricket Test, day five – live Read more Share Updated at  04.23 EDT 26m ago 04.19 EDT 4th over: England 18-0 (Banton 15, Duckett 3) Banton jumpstarts the England innings with three successive boundaries: an edge wide of slip, a classy off-drive and an even better back-foot punch through extra cover. Good lad.
 View image in fullscreen Tom Banton gets some runs on the board. Photograph: Farooq Naeem/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  04.42 EDT 30m ago 04.15 EDT 3rd over: England 5-0 (Banton 2, Duckett 3) Duckett survives a run-out chance after taking a quick single on the off side. He was just short of his ground when Arachchige’s throw bounced past the stumps at the bowler’s end.
 Another quiet over, with only one big stroke from Banton that didn’t beat the cover fielder. Sri Lanka have bowled an excellent length and England look like they want to get the measure of the pitch before they unsheath the long handle.
 Share 34m ago 04.11 EDT 2nd over: England 3-0 (Banton 1, Duckett 2) The left-armer Dilshan Madushanka continues Sri Lanka’s good start, conceding three singles. England’s openers have started cautiously and are doing their own pitch inspection.
 Share 40m ago 04.05 EDT 1st over: England 0-0 (Banton 0, Duckett 0) The stocky Asitha Fernando starts with a maiden to Tom Banton. No real swing, but no looseners either and Banton was unable to pierce the infield.
 Share 43m ago 04.02 EDT Tom Banton and Ben Duckett walk out to the middle. Banton made a blistering maiden hundred against Sri Lanka at the Oval last month.
 Share 53m ago 03.51 EDT This week’s Spin is a lovely read 
 The Spin | Writing a book with Chris Woakes showed the inner steel of the nicest man in cricket Read more Share 1h ago 03.47 EDT Bradman b Hollies 0 
 Jimmy Anderson set to retire from cricket as Lancashire opt against renewing contract Read more Share 1h ago 03.41 EDT Team news: Rashid dropped
 England make two changes from the defeat to Pakistan. Josh Tongue and Liam Dawson replaces Sonny Baker and… Adil Rashid, who of late has been nowhere near his magical best.
 Sri Lanka bring in the left-arm spinner Dunith Wellalage for the leggie Sachindu Colombage. Their team also includes the opener Avishka Fernando, who looked a star of the future when Sri Lanka stunned England at Headingley in the 2019 World Cup.
 Fernando, aged 21, made an audacious 39-ball 49 in that game. He’s had a stop-start career but I’m looking forward to seeing him again.
 England Banton, Duckett, Root, Brook (c), Cox (wk), Curran, Jacks, Overton, Dawson, Atkinson, Tongue.
 Sri Lanka Kamindu Mendis, Avishka Fernando, Kusal Mendis (c/wk), Rathnayake, Arachchige, Liyanage, Shanaka, Wellalage, Malinga, Asitha Fernando, Madushanka.
 Share 1h ago 03.34 EDT Sri Lanka win the toss and bowl
 That might not be a bad thing for England, who are better at setting targets than chasing them.
 Share 1h ago 03.30 EDT At the risk of misquoting Black Grape , it’s a big day in Gqeberha, where Australia have a helluva job on to save the second Test against South Africa. Geoff Lemon is on OBO duty.
 South Africa v Australia: second men’s cricket Test, day five – live Read more Share Updated at  03.32 EDT 1h ago 03.16 EDT Preamble
 double quotation mark There was a little girl,
 Who had a little curl,
 Right in the middle of her forehead.
 When she was good,
 She was very good indeed,
 But when she was bad she was horrid.
 The little girl with the little curl, the subject of Henry Wadsworth Longfellow’s famous poem, has plenty in common with this England team. They’re a one-day side with two faces, and we saw both during Tuesday’s defeat against Pakistan.
 England seemed to be cruising to victory, only to flunk a 300+ chase for the second time in three games. There’s no need to get carried away – that’s what social media is for – but negative patterns are never a good thing for a cricket team, especially when they involve batting collapses. After a largely positive 2026, the tame manner of Tuesday’s defeat was a setback.
 It means today’s match against Sri Lanka is, if not a must-win, then at least a need-to-win. The losers will be bottom of the tri-series at the halfway stage, with nul points and a lot of work to do. May the best team not lose.
